description: B1 DECK ON PIER FOOTINGS (DECK-FOOTINGS; docs/reference-parts/buildings.md B1 'Footings') from ONE loft.deck 1.2.0 custom feature, width 192 in (16 ft), projection 144 in, everything else the plugin's defaults: 1.1.0's B1 framing and decking, and a round pier footing under each of its 3 posts, 16 in across and 12 in deep, its top at grade, bought as 80 lb bags with a 6x6 post base each. model.json is EXACTLY the plugin's expansion with the member materials documents applies (pressure-treated southern pine framing, concrete piers); members.json is each body's member metadata with its plugin. packages/loft-plugins/tests/test_deck_footings.py pins both; services/geometry/tests/test_deck_footings_b1.py checks the cut list (3 footings, 8 bags, 3 post bases), the exported STEP and interference.
derivation: Every expectation except the mesh counts is ANALYTIC, typed from buildings.md, never from the plugin: the deck's boxes are plugin-deck-v1-b1-12x16ft's (46 boxes, 64497.75 in^3, its derivation), and the 3 piers are cylinders of radius 8 in, Z -12..0, centred on the posts at X 2.75, 96, 189.25, Y 126 (the beam line).
surface_area = the boxes' sum of 2(ab + bc + ca) plus 3 x (2 pi 8^2 + 2 pi 8 x 12) = 3 x 320 pi in^2 (bodies are separate; a pier's top touches its post, never merged) = 80945437.429734 mm^2.

centroid = volume-weighted mean of the box centres (exact rationals) and the piers' centre (X the posts' mean, 96 in; Y 126; Z -6): 2438.400000, 2097.6159085273, 567.1972689608 mm. X is symmetric about the deck's centre.
mass_g = the boxes' volume x 582.0 kg/m^3 (southern_pine_pt) + the piers' x 2400.0 kg/m^3 (concrete) = 899804.527760 g; center_of_mass weights the same centres by mass.
bounding_box: X -5.25 (the first pier, 2.75 - 8) .. 197.25 in (the last, 189.25 + 8), Y 0 .. 146.125 (the last board), Z -12 (the piers' bottoms) .. 30.
topology: 46 boxes x (6 faces, 12 edges, 1 shell) + 3 cylinders x (3 faces: two planar discs and the lateral face; 3 edges: two circles and the seam; 1 shell) = 285 faces, 561 edges, 49 shells.

MESH counts: the boxes are exact (24 vertices, 12 triangles each: 1104, 552); each pier is RECORDED from the kernel at linear deflection 0.1 mm and checked for structure: its circle split into 126 segments gives 4 x 126 - 4 = 500 triangles (2 x 126 on the side, 126 - 2 on each disc) on 4 x 126 + 2 = 506 vertices (the side's seam doubled); 1104 + 3 x 506 = 2622, 552 + 3 x 500 = 2052.
Interference none (test_deck_footings_b1): each pier's top meets its post's foot face to face at Z 0, and no two piers or members overlap.
tolerance_rationale: Measured first, then set (geometry-gates skill), as for the 1.0.0 decks: the bounds are ABSOLUTE and the part is ~1.2e9-1.5e9 mm^3 summed over separate bodies, so the double-precision sum carries ~1e-6 mm^3 of round-off. Kernel vs this derivation, measured 2026-10-28: volume -9.5e-7 (16 ft) and +1.7e-6 (20 ft) mm^3, area <= 7.5e-8 mm^2, centroid and centre of mass <= 2.3e-12 mm, mass <= 9.3e-10 g. 1e-5 is 6x the worst; a pier 1/16 in narrower moves the volume by ~3e5 mm^3 and fails by ten orders.
roundtrip_tolerance_rationale: Measured 2026-10-28: the STEP round trip re-sums the re-imported solids in another order, moving the volume by -1.2e-6 (16 ft) and -3.6e-6 (20 ft) mm^3 and the area by <= 1.1e-7 mm^2 (~2e-15 relative), below which ROUNDTRIP_TOL (1e-7 absolute) cannot reach for a sum of this size; the 1.0.0 deck drifts +3.0e-6 the same way. 1e-5 is 2.8x the worst and the 1.0.0 decks' bound; it applies to volume and area only, the centroid (<= 6.4e-12 mm) and bounds keep ROUNDTRIP_TOL.
